slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Not covered here? Ask us directly — same working day response.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Managed Detection and Response pairs security tooling with people who look at what it finds. The tooling watches for suspicious behaviour across your devices, Microsoft 365 and servers. When something looks real, a person investigates it and acts to contain it. The managed part is the bit that matters, because software on its own only produces alerts.

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: In working hours, alerts raise a ticket in our helpdesk and our own engineers investigate. Outside working hours, monitoring and first response are covered by a specialist partner who can act on anything urgent. We would rather tell you that plainly than imply we staff our own overnight security operations centre, because most providers our size do not.

slots.label: Question 3
slots.default: How is MDR different from antivirus?

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Antivirus checks whether a file matches something already known to be bad. MDR watches behaviour, which catches attacks that use no malware at all, such as someone logging in with a stolen password and using tools already present on the machine. You want both. Antivirus stops the obvious, MDR catches what walks straight past it.

slots.label: Question 4
slots.default: We have Microsoft 365 Business Premium. Isn’t that enough?

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Business Premium includes genuinely capable security tooling, and we often build on exactly that rather than selling you something extra. The gap is not the licence, it is that the alerts it generates go to nobody in particular. MDR is the layer that turns those alerts into someone investigating and responding.

slots.label: Question 5
slots.default: What happens when something is detected?

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: The affected account or device is contained first so the problem stops spreading. Then it gets investigated to establish what happened, how it got in and what it reached. You are told what we found and what we did, in language you can pass to your insurer or your board without a translator.

slots.label: Question 6
slots.default: Does MDR help with Cyber Essentials or cyber insurance?

slots.label: Paragraph 7
slots.default: Cyber Essentials does not require MDR, though the malware protection and secure configuration controls sit comfortably alongside it. Insurers are a different matter. Many now ask directly whether you have monitoring and response in place, and the answer can affect both your premium and whether a claim is paid. We hold Cyber Essentials certification ourselves and can take you through it.
